Investors from countries
including the US, China and ​India are interested in a new port
project ‌in southern Peru estimated to cost ​around $844 million,
officials said on Monday.

The ⁠port is expected to have a greater draft depth than
Chancay, the northern Peru port ‌operated by China's Cosco
Shipping Ports since late 2024, which accommodates
large vessels ‌making nonstop voyages between South ‌America ⁠and
Asia.

"Several companies have approached us," regional ⁠governor
Rohel Sanchez told reporters after signing an agreement with the
state agency Proinversion, aimed at showcasing ​the project to
domestic ‌and foreign investors.

"We have investors from the US, China and India who are very
interested," he added, without identifying the ‌specific
companies involved.

China has become a key ​investor in Peru at a time when
Washington is seeking to ⁠curb Beijing's influence in Latin
America, while the Asian nation remains a key market ‌for
Peruvian minerals.

While Corio could be a terminal for general cargo and
containers, Proinversion President Luis del Carpio did not rule
out its use for shipping minerals such as copper sourced from
the area to ‌Asia.

The government announced in September that China's ​Jinzhao
would begin construction in 2027 of a $405 million port in the
town ⁠of Marcona, in the Ica region.

Sanchez said ⁠companies from Turkey and the Netherlands have
also shown interest, as have ‌investors from South Korea
regarding technological development within the logistics park.

title: India, US and China investors eye $844 million port project in Peru
